newsitem.title: UK: UK's Brown says will cut VAT on fuel.
newsitem.headline: UK's Brown says will cut VAT on fuel.

text.p: Britain's Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown said on Tuesday he would fulfil Labour's manifesto pledge to cut VAT on heating fuel to five percent from eight.

"It is the law. We will be able to do it. I am absolutely certain it is possible and we will do it and I have already said we are going to legislate in the first Budget," he told a news conference, shortly after sanctioning a quarter-point interest rate rise.
"The VAT cut will be with people by the time they receive their winter fuel bills," Brown said.
Earlier on Tuesday, a European Commission spokesman said Labour's pledge to cut VAT on fuel may meet with opposition in the EU.
"The spirit of the (EU's VAT) directive was to bring normal rates together. The fact you should reduce (VAT on fuel) goes against that objective," spokeswoman Betty Olivi told a news conference.
